topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course context, her background, and the key learning outcomes regarding cancer causation and carcinogen appraisal.

topics.label: Intrinsic versus Environmental Drivers of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological basis of cancer as a genetic disease and evaluate the relative contributions of stochastic endogenous mutations versus environmental exposures and epidemiology.

topics.label: Mutagenic Mechanisms of Pathogens and Environmental Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific infectious, physical, and chemical agents interact with host metabolism to induce DNA damage and oncogenic transformation.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Context
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic factors such as tumor promoters, chronic inflammation, and tissue developmental timing enable initiated cells to progress into cancer.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Evaluating Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the analytical, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro models used to detect mutagenic signatures and establish carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Conclusion and Everyday Risk-Benefit Evaluation
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by summarising the main themes and reflecting on how individuals and society navigate carcinogen risks versus benefits.
